label: Integration And Stokes' Theorem
notes: Open by placing the chapter at the start of the surface integration thread. The learner has just met surfaces, tangent planes, induced metrics, and area density. This lecture asks what must be added so an integral becomes coordinate independent and orientation sensitive.

label: Why Ordinary Density Is Not Enough
notes: Motivate differential forms by contrasting a scalar density with an oriented measuring device. A scalar can tell us how much material sits at a point, but a form also knows which tangent directions were fed into it and how the orientation of those directions affects the sign.

label: Lecture Route
notes: Preview the four moves in the lecture. First pull back an oriented measurement to a coordinate domain. Then integrate one-forms along curves and two-forms over surface patches. After that, enforce the boundary orientation rule. The final move is Stokes' theorem, where a boundary integral is explained by an interior derivative.

label: Two-Forms Measure Oriented Area
notes: Use this slide to define the operational meaning of a two-form. It takes an ordered pair of tangent vectors and returns a signed area-like value. Reversing the order flips the sign, and feeding in dependent vectors gives zero, so the form reacts exactly to the oriented parallelogram.

label: Pullback Moves The Measurement
notes: Explain pullback as the act of moving the measuring rule to the parameter square. We do not push little rectangles blindly onto the surface; instead, the surface map differentiates coordinate vectors, and the original form evaluates those transported tangent vectors.

label: Surface Integrals Use The Chart But Do Not Belong To It
notes: The chart supplies parameters and a Jacobian-like area signal, but the integral is intended to describe the geometric patch. The displayed formula is a compact way of saying that the two-form eats the two coordinate tangent vectors before the ordinary du dv integration happens.

label: One-Forms Measure Tangent Motion
notes: Shift from surfaces to curves. A one-form does not merely count length; it pairs with the curve velocity. Reparametrization changes the speed and time variable together, so the measured line integral remains the same when the orientation is preserved.

label: Boundary Orientation Is Part Of The Data
notes: Stress that the direction on a boundary is not a sketching preference. Once the surface orientation is chosen, the induced boundary orientation is fixed. For a region with a hole, the outer loop and inner loop run in opposite senses because the oriented surface must stay on the same side of the moving boundary tangent.

label: Exterior Derivative Detects Local Circulation
notes: Introduce the exterior derivative through a small-loop test. If a one-form accumulates nonzero circulation around tiny rectangles, the normalized limiting density is a two-form. This is the local interior quantity that Stokes will integrate. Emphasize that the sign depends on the same orientation convention used for the tiny boundary loop.

label: Stokes' Theorem
notes: State the theorem as a balance law. The left side is the measurement made by walking around the boundary, and the right side is the accumulated local circulation over the oriented surface. The theorem is powerful because every coordinate and triangulation used to compute either side is auxiliary.

label: Disk Example
notes: Work the disk example slowly because it fixes the sign convention. The one-form one half times minus y dx plus x dy measures angular circulation. Its exterior derivative is the standard area form, so the boundary integral around the positively oriented unit circle equals the area of the disk.

label: Annulus Sign Check
notes: Use the annulus to make the hole orientation concrete. The exterior derivative integrates over the material annulus. The outer boundary contributes positively with the usual counterclockwise direction, while the inner boundary contributes with the opposite orientation, subtracting the missing disk.

label: Notebook Diagnostics
notes: Connect the theorem to the chapter notebook checks. The computational habit is to change a parametrization, boundary direction, or sampling grid and then watch the invariant. A small residual supports the implementation; a sign flip or large residual points to an orientation or regularity mistake.

label: Takeaways
notes: Close with the conceptual chain. Forms are measuring devices for tangent data. Pullback makes them computable in coordinates. Orientation determines sign. Stokes says the derivative inside the surface accounts exactly for the accumulated measurement along the boundary.
